A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their text, equations, figures, table, and complete appendices support reliable comparison. The Gaussian-mixture and computing-resources appendices are retained under new letters.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic simulations in Appendix B.3 and image-generation experiments on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet, including quantitative results in Table 1 and the figures.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds EDM-2 latent-diffusion experiments with quantitative and qualitative outcomes in Appendix G, Figures 38–39.

M1.justification: The CFG decomposition, mean-shift initialization, and nonlinear Jacobian/CPC guidance procedures are unchanged. Appendix G applies existing guidance methods to EDM-2. Suggested new training objectives remain future work.

E1.justification: Both versions cover CIFAR-10, ImageNet class-conditioned generation, and synthetic Gaussian simulations. The added EDM-2 experiments revisit golden retriever, already evaluated in v1; they change model configuration and resolution without introducing a new dataset, class, or task.

E2.justification: Existing comparator membership is retained. Appendix G reuses actual CFG, linear CFG, mean-shift, and positive/negative CPC guidance, plus the existing nonlinear comparison with conditional-PC guidance and no guidance. EDM-2 supplies another backbone rather than a competing guidance method.

E3.justification: Appendix G adds a 512×512 EDM-2 configuration with 50,000 golden-retriever images per method for FD_DINOv2. Figure 38 tests guidance strengths 0, 5, 10, 15, and 20 over noise levels [16.02, 80); Figure 39 uses strength 8 at noise level 1.502. Existing experiments retain their settings.

E4.justification: Figures 38–39 add limited tests of whether the component-level findings extend to latent diffusion: isolating guidance components across strengths and contrasting positive-CPC with conditional-PC guidance at low noise. The extensive existing analyses in Appendices D–F remain.

E5.justification: The existing averaging over ten randomly initialized trajectories in Figure 25 is unchanged. The new experiments retain point-estimate reporting without adding repeated-run summaries, confidence intervals, significance tests, or seed information. Their 50,000-image counts describe evaluation samples.

E6.justification: v2 adds EDM-2 FD_DINOv2 curves and generated examples in Figures 38–39, including qualitative evidence of CPC sharpening and conditional-PC oversaturation. Existing results, including Table 1, are unchanged. The additions use different model and resolution settings, so they are not same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: Assumption 1, Theorems 1–2, the ODE proofs, and the Gaussian-mixture derivation are retained. The Gaussian-mixture material moves from Appendix G to H; expanded explanatory prose introduces no new formal result.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and central conclusion retain the class-specificity gap, three-component CFG mechanism, and connection between linear and nonlinear guidance. EDM-2 provides additional supporting evidence; the proposed training-objective direction does not redefine the core contribution.

C2.justification: Section 3.1 adds the qualification that CFG would distort an already-correct conditional distribution. Section 4.2 strengthens the existing non-equivalence caveat by stating that actual nonlinear CFG is more stable and consistent than the heuristic. Section 5 adds implications for training objectives that encourage class-specific features.

D1.justification: Section 5 explicitly identifies the existing main-text model as pixel-space EDM-1 at 64×64. Appendix G documents EDM-2 resolution and guidance hyperparameters. The promised code release and A100 GPU disclosure remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Kalimeris et al., 'SGD on Neural Networks Learns Functions of Increasing Complexity,' as reference 28 to support the simplicity-bias discussion. Other cited works and the central positioning relative to Gaussian CFG analyses and contrastive PCA are retained.

P1.justification: Sections 3.1 and 4.2 receive localized rewrites and expanded explanations, with additions to the conclusion and acknowledgments. Appendix G is inserted and subsequent appendices are relabeled, while the main narrative and section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 38–39, comprising an EDM-2 component comparison, metric plot, and nonlinear-guidance image grid. Figure 9 moves from page 12 to page 13, and nearby material reflows. Existing figures and Table 1 retain their displays.

improvement.justification: The added EDM-2 experiments modestly strengthen support for the mechanism beyond v1's pixel-space neural-model experiments. The explicit acknowledgment that actual CFG is more stable than the heuristic also better qualifies the conclusions. The gain remains limited because the added latent-diffusion validation focuses on one class.
